answer: One concrete defense is proof of unique storage. Each new agent is assigned its own random data shard, a kind of digital relic it must keep intact, and peers request random slices of it at unpredictable times. A farm running a thousand identities has to hold a thousand distinct shards, so its cost grows linearly instead of hiding in an ocean of cheap clones. No ivory-tower auditor is needed: any established peer can check a slice against the shard's published hash.
